verdict: No demonstrated query-boundary escape in current local topology; production topology and current full identity trace remain unqualified
topology: Current saved public wallet configuration selects loopback53877/v1/node, remoteProver:null and native/PXE proofsfalse. This is local development, not evidence of a remote prover operator.
bootstrap starts query service with exact net.nodeUrl; private-query admits fixed loopback upstream and forwards approved parsed method arguments.
network constructs native AztecNodeService in process, localL1 RPC and p2pdisabled. Installed node factory creates local archiver and assigns logsSource:archiver.

NodeLogsProvider resolves reference then calls local logsSource; archiver data_source_base delegates tag reads to its local indexed log store. No per-tag miss path forwards personal queries to an external node.
PublicL1/blob ingestion is distinct from per-user tag lookups; localAnvil is selected. This source review does not assert all OS/network egress monitored.

documentedTrust.requirement: Operate fullnode, persistent worldstate, archiver, contract-data and logs in the same explicitly disclosed trusted prover boundary; do not forward user-specific misses to boardbackend or another node. Matching URL/network does not establish operator identity.
documentedTrust.interpretation: This extends the explicitly allowed witness trust only by keeping query processing inside that same operator boundary, not by declaring arbitrary node operators trusted. Local development currently has one operator; production deployment must demonstrate containment and upstream behavior.

batchSemantics: PXE LogService groups tag retrieval requests by range and contract, derives siloed private tags, then getAllPrivateLogsByTags batches up to installedMAX_RPC_LEN and requests includeEffects:true.

Installed LogResultSchema returns block/hash/txHash/logposition and optional noteHashes/nullifiers. The query operator can associate each requested tag with matching public transaction effects and group requested interests in one batch. This is stronger than pure network timing.

A matching tag response does not itself prove caller can decrypt/owns every matching note/name; batches include discovery candidates and potentially other sender/recipient relations. Current method-only counts cannot establish that one observed batch contained multiple owned-name registration notes. No actual cross-name ownership disclosure is claimed.
smallestCompliantPath: Retain current local/trusted gateway+localarchiver and existing cryptographically checked SDK APIs. Do not replace ordinary note discovery with a new archive scanner solely from counts.

For remote acceptance, use the existing deployment runbook topology and one controlled operator for proving/query/worldstate/archive, verify fixed ingestion and no user-specific forwarding. Independent node access is not an allowed fallback.
Keep specialized cold preference recovery using canonical compact ranges/local processing and zero-tag window checks. Separate its observations from ordinary account-status/signing discovery.

When next required multiidentity flow runs, reuse existing known-role wire/effect projection and receiver reconciliation to answer whether actual request/result linkage groups ownednames; label opaque/response/native gaps. No additional financial or expensive acceptance run merely for a new observer.
decision: Evidence/deployment-qualification gap today, not sufficient evidence for an application defect or broad rewrite. A demonstrated personal query forwarded to a separate untrusted operator would be a concrete blocker requiring routing/deployment repair.
constraints: Read-only files/source only, no live network/browser/services/credential discovery.
